labels.label: [5.B] Bieberbach (prose, Barbot §5.1, label bieb)

hypotheses.note: as IsDiscreteEucl: forall x R, finitely many gamma in Gamma with dist (gamma x) x <= R; proved equivalent to mathlib's ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul Gamma E, and one base point suffices

L(Gamma) in O(E). Convention note, NOT an erratum: Barbot reserves 'isometry' for orientation-preserving maps (l.476-481; also l.1775 'holonomy in SO(R^n/U)'), so SO(n) is consistent as written. O(E) is taken because the downstream use at l.2305 restricts an SO0(1,n-1) element to a spacelike U, and that restriction can reverse U's orientation.

hypotheses.paper: L(Gamma) finite => kernel of L|Gamma of finite index
hypotheses.note: discreteness of Gamma not used for the finite-index part; it is used only for the lattice / Z^k part
any finite-dimensional real inner product space E; dropped where unused (the unipotent lemmas, the IsDiscreteEucl criteria, and both upgrade theorems)

findings: l.1732-1733: 'the kernel of the restriction morphism Gamma -> Isom(U) is a finite index subgroup of Gamma_nd' is false as written: that kernel is the pointwise stabiliser of U in Gamma, which for a discrete Gamma lies in the stabiliser of a point and is therefore FINITE, so it has finite index only when Gamma is finite. The step the argument needs is that Gamma_nd itself acts on U by translations (the closing 'unipotent elements of Isom(U) are translations', proved here as actsByTranslationsOn_of_unipotent), followed by an extra step the paper omits: the finite kernel of Gamma_nd -> Isom(U) has to be avoided by a further finite-index subgroup (finite-by-Z^j is virtually Z^j) before 'free abelian' follows.

l.2611-2612 ('up to finite index, there is a unique maximal affine subspace U on which Gamma acts by translations'): the phrase 'up to finite index' alone does not determine U. Example: the screw motion g of R^3, rotation by 2*pi/m about the z-axis composed with the translation e_z, acts by translations only on the axis, while its index-m subgroup <g^m> (translation by m*e_z) acts by translations on all of R^3. In §5.1 itself the U is canonical (l.1729-1730): it is the unique maximal unipotent subspace of the specific subgroup Gamma_nd (bthm:unip's uniqueness); in the example Gamma_nd = <g^m> and U = R^3. For a FIXED finite-index Gamma' the maximal subspace is unique (it is the translation locus of Gamma'; formalized as BieberbachMaxConclusion). Only the phrasing at l.2611 is ambiguous.

Correction of the previous report: the downstream uses do NOT need existence only. Maximality is spent at l.2611-2614 (U is timelike only because a MAXIMAL U contains the direction Delta_0 fixed by L(Gamma) in SO(n-1); a spacelike line for Gamma = Z acting by spacelike translations does not) and at l.2889-2891 ('since U_0 is the *maximal* lambda(Gamma)-unipotent subspace, it must contain every U_t', about the U produced at l.2877). Cocompactness is spent at l.1772-1775 ('a twisted product of a flat torus Gamma\U by R^n/U') and in the crystallographic corollary l.1737-1749 (reasoning with dim U). Both forms are now PROVED from the weak BieberbachI (bieberbachMaxConclusion_of_bieberbachConclusion, mem_direction_of_fixed, bieberbachCocompactConclusion_of_bieberbachMaxConclusion, virtuallyFree_of_bieberbachCocompactConclusion).

l.1772-1775 ('the argument in the preceding section actually show that any locally euclidean manifold is a twisted product of a flat torus Gamma\U by R^n/U'): the U must be the COCOMPACT subspace (translation vectors spanning U), which in general is not the maximal unipotent subspace of the preceding argument. Example: Gamma = Z acting by a translation on R^2; L(Gamma) is trivial, Gamma_nd = Gamma, its maximal unipotent subspace is R^2, and Gamma\R^2 is a cylinder, not a torus; the statement holds with U the line spanned by the translation vector. The maximal and the cocompact U are different subspaces, so no single U serves l.2611 and l.1773 at once.

Line numbers: in papers/barbot/legacy/labeled/GHFspace.tex §5 starts at l.1688 and §5.1 ([5.B]) runs l.1690-1749 (the dispatch and docs/BARBOT.md give l.1667-1726 / l.1667-1822, which are the orig/ numbers). The REPORT and the docstring use the labelled file's numbers.
questions: Discreteness (l.1723, and wherever 'discrete group of isometries' is used): the reading taken is IsDiscreteEucl, i.e. uniformly locally finite orbits, which is the same as properly discontinuous (proved) and, classically, as discrete in the compact-open topology of Isom(E) (not formalized, because mathlib puts no topology on E ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] E). Is that the intended meaning?

Reading of 'up to finite index, the unique maximal U' (l.2611) taken: a finite-index Gamma' NORMAL in Gamma, and U the greatest affine subspace on which Gamma' acts by translations (unique for that Gamma', Gamma-invariant by normality). 'Flat torus Gamma\U' (l.1773) is read as: Gamma' normal of finite index acting effectively by translations on a Gamma-invariant U whose translation vectors span U's direction (so Gamma' ≅ Z^{dim U} under discreteness). Downstream WPs should keep the weak BieberbachI as their hypothesis and call the two upgrade lemmas. Are these the intended readings?

kb_proposals: At this mathlib pin E ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] E has a Group instance but NO MulAction on E and NO topology: Flat/Bieberbach.lean adds the action as a SCOPED instance Causal.Flat.instMulActionAffineIsometryEquiv (active inside namespace Causal.Flat or after `open Causal.Flat`); reuse it, do not redefine it. Discreteness is the metric IsDiscreteEucl, proved equivalent to ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul.

Discrete subgroups as lattices are already in mathlib: instModuleFree_of_discrete_submodule, instModuleFinite_of_discrete_submodule, Real.finrank_eq_int_finrank_of_discrete. To use them on an AddSubgroup S, give the instance explicitly with `letI : DiscreteTopology (AddSubgroup.toIntSubmodule S) := h`: it is defeq to S's, but instance search will not find it.
A unipotent linear isometry fixes every vector it moves unipotently, pointwise and with no invariance hypothesis (linearIsometry_apply_eq_self_of_unipotent).

Bieberbach has two different 'U's: the maximal one (greatest translation subspace of a normal finite-index Gamma', needed for 'U contains every L(Gamma)-fixed direction') and the cocompact one (translation vectors span U, needed for 'Gamma\U is a torus'). For Z acting by a translation on R^2 they are R^2 and a line. Keep the weak BieberbachI as the hypothesis and call bieberbachMaxConclusion_of_bieberbachConclusion / bieberbachCocompactConclusion_of_bieberbachMaxConclusion.

For X : Subgroup K, (X.map K.subtype).subgroupOf K = X is Subgroup.comap_map_eq_self_of_injective K.subtype_injective X (subgroupOf is comap of the subtype); the normal core of a finite-index subgroupOf is finite index by instance (Subgroup.finiteIndex_normalCore).
